findings.reproduction: Add to the file: `const model = getModel(PROMPT_REFINER_EXECUTION_MODEL_PIN.modelId); const pricing = getModelPricingProfile(PROMPT_REFINER_EXECUTION_MODEL_PIN.modelId); assert.ok(promptRefinerExecutionContractProblems({ model: { ...model, inputUsdPerMillionTokens: 99 }, pricing }).includes("effective_input_price_mismatch")); assert.ok(promptRefinerExecutionContractProblems({ model: { ...model, maxOutputTokens: 100 }, pricing }).includes("effective_output_cap_below_contract"));` then run `node --conditions=react-server --import tsx --test tests/promptRefinerExecutionContract.test.mjs`. It passes today, showing the behaviour is correct but untested; deleting lines 202-227 of lib/promptRefinerExecutionContract.ts with the env tests removed would leave the registry-row path silent.

findings.claim: The `{ concurrency: false }` option added to these process.env-mutating tests is a no-op that suggests a serialization guarantee it does not give, since node:test's `concurrency` configures a test's own subtests (default 1) and these tests have none — the real isolation comes from `withIsolatedPriceEnv` plus the root's default sequential execution.
findings.reproduction: Remove `{ concurrency: false }` from all seven tests and run `node --conditions=react-server --import tsx --test tests/promptRefinerExecutionContract.test.mjs`: the suite passes identically, so the option changes no scheduling. Conversely it would still not help if the root were made concurrent, because it only bounds subtests of each leaf.
